Both bottlenecks are near the structural floor for this algorithm. Suggested next directions: (1) the now-dominant geomean contributors are n=2048 (73k us) and n=4096 (48k us), still on geqrf -- these are tiny-batch (8,2) so the batched-panel approach starves SMs; they need within-matrix parallelism (worker 2's brief). CholeskyQR2 large-n path investigated and found INFEASIBLE on this hardware/these shapes; submission kept at brief-0 best (no regression, geqrf fallback retained for n=2048/4096). EVIDENCE: benchmark large-n shapes are NOT well-conditioned -- cond(A)~9e3-8e4 (n2048) and 6e4-5.7e5 (n4096), so cond(A^T A)~6e9-3e11 >> 1/eps32 (8e6). (a) FP32 Gram Cholesky breaks (non-PD) on EVERY benchmark large-n matrix. (b) Shifted CholeskyQR3 (shift~100*eps*max diagG) factors without breakdown but produces an INVALID QR: factor residual 248-365 >> gate ~0.01 (small singular values lost below FP32). (c) FP64 CholeskyQR2 is numerically correct (all gates pass, sfr~1e-3, sorth~0.1, breakdown correctly detected on rankdef/upper) BUT ~10x SLOWER than geqrf: FP64 Gram alone 179k us vs geqrf 50k us for n4096 (Blackwell sm_120 has no fast FP64 tensor cores, ~1/64 FP32 rate). De-risked orhr_col reconstruction per consultant: derived+verified in FP64 that M=I-Q*diag(s), no-pivot LU(M)=L*U gives V=L, tau=diag(U), R_final=diag(s)*R, producing valid (H,tau) (checker validates QR invariants, not geqrf sign-match). Caveat: torch.linalg.lu_factor PIVOTS, so a no-pivot LU kernel is required. Metric unchanged 5884.298 (19.68x).

I DID de-risk the consultant's #1 risk (orhr_col): derived & verified in FP64 that with s=-sign(diag(Q)), M=I-Q*diag(s), a NO-PIVOT LU(M)=L*U yields V=L (unit-lower Householder vectors), tau=diag(U), R_final=diag(s)*R, and this passes the checker (which validates QR invariants, not a geqrf sign-match -- any valid Householder rep is accepted). Gotcha for a future attempt: torch.linalg.lu_factor PIVOTS, so a custom no-pivot LU (Triton/torch) is needed; the Python-loop no-pivot LU is O(n) launches and unusably slow at n=4096. CONCLUSION per the consultant's own escape hatch: the cheap CholeskyQR path is provably valid for NO shape in the active benchmark set (all large-n have cond(A)>>4000), so keeping geqrf is correct.
